explanation: In South Korean social gatherings, hugging or cheek-kissing, especially between acquaintances, is generally considered inappropriate; bowing and handshaking are the expected greetings. Public displays of affection between opposite-sex people are seen as rude, though same-sex hugging and hand-holding are acceptable. Greeting strangers with familiarity such as a hug is viewed as too forward.
local_tip: At a social gathering, offer a slight bow and a handshake (supporting your right forearm with your left hand when greeting someone older or senior) instead of a hug.
regional_note: Same-sex hugging is generally acceptable, while opposite-sex hugging is considered rude; formality increases with age and seniority.

also_check.note: Bowing is standard; hugging acquaintances is uncommon and can feel intrusive.
The wai greeting is preferred; hugging is reserved for close friends and family.
La bise (cheek kisses) is common among acquaintances, but hugging is less standard and varies by region and relationship.
